title: Where Am I? Semantic Map Grounding via Vision-Language Models for Multi-Modal Localization
summary: We address robot localization in GPS-denied indoor environments by reframing it as a semantic reasoning task rather than a geometric estimation problem. Motivated by how humans localize using object-level cues and labeled maps, we ask whether a vision-language model, given a front camera image, a polar LiDAR scan, and a top-down semantic grid map, can infer the robot pose. We fine-tune Qwen2.5-VL-7B with LoRA and attach a lightweight regression head that predicts continuous pose coordinates (x, y, theta) directly from the final hidden state, bypassing text generation. Training uses a composite position-and-direction loss with curriculum learning on a custom Gazebo dataset of 120,112 samples and 527 scenes. On the in-distribution test set of 18,017 samples, the model achieves 98.23 percent position accuracy, 98.00 percent direction accuracy, 96.75 percent full pose accuracy, a mean position error of 0.11 m, and a mean orientation error of 5.7 degrees at 0.62 s per sample. Position accuracy drops by only 7.2 percentage points on seven unseen object categories, reaching 90.99 percent, supporting semantic spatial reasoning rather than appearance memorization. With incomplete maps, fine-tuning recovers performance to 93.72 percent position accuracy, showing adaptability to stale or partial map information. Two ablations highlight cross-modal complementarity. Without LiDAR, using only camera and map inputs, position accuracy remains 95.06 percent, only 3.2 percentage points below the full system. However, when the camera sees no visible objects in a wall-facing view, LiDAR sustains 92.33 percent position accuracy, compared with 70.74 percent when neither LiDAR nor visible objects are available. This shows that LiDAR becomes the primary localization signal when camera semantics are unavailable and provides a reliable fallback under occlusion or sparse layouts.
tldr: This paper reframes robot localization in GPS-denied indoor environments as a semantic reasoning task, fine-tuning a vision-language model (Qwen2.5-VL-7B) with LoRA and a regression head to predict continuous pose from camera, LiDAR, and semantic map inputs. The method achieves high accuracy on seen scenes and demonstrates robustness to unseen objects and incomplete maps, highlighting the complementarity of visual and LiDAR modalities.
tldr_zh: 本文将GPS受限室内环境中的机器人定位重新定义为语义推理任务，通过LoRA微调视觉语言模型（Qwen2.5-VL-7B）并附加回归头，从相机、激光雷达和语义地图输入中直接预测连续位姿。该方法在已知场景中达到高精度，并展示了对未见物体和不完整地图的鲁棒性，突出了视觉与激光雷达模态的互补性。
summary_zh: 我们将GPS信号缺失的室内环境中的机器人定位问题重构为语义推理任务，而非几何估计问题。受人类通过物体级线索和标注地图进行定位的启发，我们探究视觉语言模型能否通过前视摄像头图像、极坐标激光雷达扫描图与俯视语义栅格地图推断出机器人位姿。采用LoRA方法微调Qwen2.5-VL-7B模型，并附加轻量级回归头，直接从最终隐藏状态预测连续位姿坐标(x, y, theta)，绕过文本生成过程。训练采用复合位置-方向损失函数，配合课程学习策略，在包含120,112个样本和527个场景的自定义Gazebo数据集上进行。在18,017个样本的分布内测试集上，模型达到98.23%的位置精度、98.00%的方向精度、96.75%的完整位姿精度，平均位置误差0.11米，平均方向误差5.7度，单样本处理时间0.62秒。在七类未见物体类别上，位置精度仅下降7.2个百分点（达90.99%），验证了模型依赖语义空间推理而非外观记忆。面对不完整地图时，微调可将位置精度恢复至93.72%，展现出对陈旧或部分地图信息的适应性。两项消融实验揭示了跨模态互补性：无激光雷达仅用摄像头和地图输入时，位置精度保持95.06%，仅比完整系统低3.2个百分点；但当摄像头面对墙面视角无可见物体时，激光雷达支撑的定位精度达92.33%，相比之下，当激光雷达与可见物体均不可用时精度仅为70.74%。这表明当摄像头语义信息缺失时，激光雷达成为主要定位信号，并在遮挡或稀疏布局场景下提供可靠的后备方案。

title: ELMP: Efficient Learning for Motion Planning via Analytical Policy Gradients
summary: Neural Motion Planners (NMPs) enable fast reactive motion generation, but adapting them to new environments typically requires recollecting large expert datasets, which is computationally prohibitive. We propose ELMP, a framework for data-efficient adaptation via self-supervised fine-tuning. Rather than generating additional expert trajectories with expensive global planners, ELMP directly optimizes the policy through a differentiable kinematic layer using dense collision, target-reaching, and smoothness objectives. This replaces expert data generation with rapid problem sampling, reducing per-sample adaptation cost by roughly two orders of magnitude. To further support robust generalization across changing kinematic chains, we introduce a mechanism to explicitly encode tool geometry via point clouds. Benchmarked against classical and neural baselines, ELMP achieves an 84.8% average success rate with orders-of-magnitude lower cold-start latency than classical methods. In unseen environments, self-supervised fine-tuning improves success rate from 57.3% (zero-shot) to 89.8%, removing the data collection bottleneck. Our approach maintains millisecond-level inference latency and is validated on a physical Franka Emika Panda robot.
tldr: This paper introduces ELMP, a framework that enables data-efficient adaptation of Neural Motion Planners (NMPs) to new environments and kinematic chains by replacing expensive expert data generation with self-supervised fine-tuning via a differentiable kinematic layer and dense collision objectives, achieving high success rates with orders-of-magnitude lower cost.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了ELMP框架，通过可微运动学层和密集碰撞目标的自监督微调，替代昂贵的专家数据生成，实现了神经运动规划器在新环境和运动链上的数据高效适应，以数量级更低的成本获得了高成功率。
summary_zh:
摘要：
神经运动规划器（NMPs）能够实现快速的反应式运动生成，但将其适应于新环境通常需要重新收集大量专家数据集，这在计算上代价过高。我们提出ELMP框架，一种通过自监督微调实现数据高效适应的方案。ELMP并非依赖昂贵的全局规划器生成额外的专家轨迹，而是通过可微运动学层，利用密集碰撞、目标到达和平滑性目标函数直接优化策略。该方法用快速问题采样替代专家数据生成，将单个样本的适应成本降低约两个数量级。为进一步支持跨变化运动链的鲁棒泛化，我们引入一种通过点云显式编码工具几何结构的机制。与经典方法和神经基线方法的基准测试表明，ELMP平均成功率达到84.8%，且冷启动延迟比经典方法低数个数量级。在未见环境中，自监督微调将成功率从57.3%（零样本）提升至89.8%，消除了数据收集瓶颈。本方法保持毫秒级推理延迟，并在物理Franka Emika Panda机器人上得到验证。
